stem:
Tushar has two $6$ cm by $2$ cm rectangles. He joins them along a shared $2$ cm edge to make one $12$ cm by $2$ cm rectangle and asks how the perimeter changes.

One or more options may be correct. Which two claims are both correct?

options.text: After the join, the perimeter is the outer boundary of the $12$ cm by $2$ cm rectangle, which is $28$ cm.
The perimeter stays $32$ cm, the sum of the perimeters of the two separate rectangles.
The shared $2$ cm edge is not part of the new outside boundary, so the perimeter is less than the sum of the separate perimeters.
The perimeter is the printed label joined arrangement.

teacher.key_rationale: Separate perimeters sum to 32 cm. Joining along a 2 cm edge removes 2 cm from each piece's boundary, so the new outer perimeter is 28 cm. Keeping the separate sum omits the new arrangement. The phrase joined arrangement is not a length.
